plan.palette_reason: Deep and bright marsh greens unify the robot armour, while warm gold strongly accents the eye and sniper scope.

body.why: Bright green establishes the main painted armour mass.

head.why: Matches the torso so the robot reads as one machine.

eye_housing.why: A black socket gives the eye maximum contrast.

eye.why: Gold remains highly visible as a filled eye pixel block.

cannon_beak.why: Dark green separates the rifle silhouette from the head.

scope.why: Gold makes the small sniper accessory survive reduction.

neck.why: Shadowed ribbing clearly divides head and torso.

wing.why: Dark green distinguishes the near wing from the mid-green body.

tail_feather_back.why: The rear tail is reduced to a shadow silhouette.

leg_front.why: Dark green preserves the visible support leg and foot.

leg_back.why: The farther leg reads as a recessed shadow.

priority.why: The single bright eye is the primary character cue.
The extra-long rifle profile defines both snipe and sniper.
Its dark ring keeps the eye readable against the head.
The top-mounted optic reinforces the sniper concept.
It anchors the eye, beak and scope.
The long wading leg and toes establish the marsh-bird stance.
The near wing supplies the bird-like side-view shape.
A small rear projection helps preserve the bird silhouette.
The narrow connector separates head from torso when space permits.
The large torso can surrender edge pixels without disappearing.
This hidden limb is least necessary and may merge into shadow.

plan.summary: At 16 px, preserve the bright eye in its black socket, the extremely long straight rifle-beak, top scope, rounded torso and at least one long wading leg with a foot.

significance.name: body
significance.reason: The torso supplies the snipe's round mass but is already large enough and should surrender pixels to identifying features.

significance.name: head
significance.reason: The head frames the eye and weapon but remains readable as a small rounded mass without enlargement.

significance.name: eye_housing
significance.reason: The socket strengthens the machine and sniper reading, but enlarging it would crowd the eye and distort the head.

significance.name: eye
significance.reason: The eye must retain a distinct 1-by-2-pixel mark at every size but must never be enlarged beyond proportional size.

overrides.why: user: eyes are fine at proportional size; never enlarge, only floor at two separate >= 1x2 rects

significance.name: cannon_beak
significance.character: long snipe bill shaped as a rifle barrel
significance.reason: This is the primary snipe-sniper cue, so it must project far left and preserve a visibly broader muzzle at 16 pixels.

significance.name: scope
significance.reason: A short horizontal block above the head is a compact secondary cue that the beak is a firearm rather than an ordinary bill.

significance.name: neck
significance.character: mechanical connector between head and torso
significance.reason: The neck clarifies construction at larger sizes but may compress or disappear without harming the core silhouette.

significance.name: wing
significance.reason: The wing supports the bird reading but is a broad low-priority region that can yield pixels to the weapon and eye.

significance.name: tail_feather_back
significance.reason: The tail helps the avian silhouette but is not important enough to compete with the long beak at the smallest size.

significance.name: leg_front
significance.character: long thin wading leg and foot
significance.reason: Its proportional length already conveys a wader, while uniform enlargement would thicken it and worsen merging with the other leg.

significance.name: leg_back
significance.character: second wading leg and offset foot
significance.reason: The rear leg supports the wading-bird stance, but enlargement cannot preserve its separation from the nearer leg and would increase collisions.

significance_summary: At 16 pixels the creature is recognised by an exaggerated long rifle-beak with a broad muzzle, a visible top scope, a floored single eye, a round body, and long proportional wading legs.
